title: Let a closed dashboard leave memory

blocks.text: The operations console opens a dashboard per team, and each open dashboard forwards its team's alerts (`"billing: 12 failed captures"`) to the team's chat channel. By design, the forwarding keeps going after a dashboard is closed: the team still wants its alerts, and the alert feed has no way to remove a listener. A heap dump after a day of use shows every dashboard ever opened still in memory, 32 MB each.
Write `alertForwarder()` in `src/main/java/practice/Dashboard.java`: the listener that sends each alert about the dashboard's team to its channel.
When you're done, a team's alerts reach its channel and nothing else's, and a closed dashboard can be garbage-collected while its alerts keep arriving. About five lines.

cases.says: an open dashboard forwards its own team's alerts to its channel, and no other team's
once nothing but the alert feed refers to it, a dashboard can be garbage-collected
a collected dashboard's team still gets its alerts, so the listener holds the channel and the team, not the dashboard

origin.section: A Lambda Keeps Its Object Alive Only When It Uses `this` or an Instance Member

concepts: A lambda captures this only when its body uses a field or an instance method without a qualifier; registered in a long-lived list, it keeps its whole object reachable, while one that uses local copies does not.
